clue.text: Eg Easter eggs served in stewed lamb's feet

indicators.note: food served in a dish sits inside it, so the eggs go inside the other letters
stewed food is cooked down and broken up, so these letters are mixed up

parts.note: ova is the Latin plural for eggs

explanation.surface: A grotesque recipe: eggs dished up inside a stew of lamb's feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eg Easter' is the definition by example: Easter is the best-known festival whose date moves. 'stewed' gives the anagram, and 'served in' places the eggs inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Easter's date shifts from year to year, making it the classic example of a church festival that is not fixed.

clue.text: Moved on, having anchored outside mouth of Tyne

indicators.note: the anchored word wraps around the outside of the river's opening letter

parts.note: a boat anchored or tied up is moored

indicators.note: a river's mouth is where it begins its exit, taken here as its first letter

explanation.surface: A boat weighs anchor at the mouth of the Tyne and heads off.
explanation.definitionFit: Travelling on by car or motorboat is to have driven, a straightforward synonym for moving along.

clue.text: Rattle's very angry about Brahms overture

indicators.note: the angry word goes about, that is around, the composer's first letter

parts.note: irate means angry

indicators.note: an overture opens a work, so only the first letter of the composer is used

explanation.surface: Conductor Simon Rattle is furious about how a Brahms overture went.
explanation.walkthrough: Rattle looks like the conductor Sir Simon Rattle, but here it is a verb meaning to shake.
explanation.definitionFit: To rattle is to shake rapidly and noisily, which is to quiver or shudder back and forth.

clue.text: Hay maybe spoils a brand new church

indicators.note: to spoil something is to ruin its form, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: CE stands for the Church of England

explanation.surface: A wet hay crop ruins a smart new church, a farming scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'spoils' rearranges A BRAND into BARNDA. A hay, or hey, is an old country dance, hence 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: The hay is a traditional rustic dance with interweaving figures, an example of a folk gathering held in a farm building.

clue.text: Essex pathologist welcomes exile

indicators.note: the two words welcome the answer in, holding it among their letters

explanation.surface: A forensic scientist in Essex takes in a banished person.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living outside their native country is an emigrant, close in sense to one banished abroad.

clue.text: Charm upright old guy in the French way

indicators.note: in a down clue, standing upright means the letters run upwards, read backwards
the old guy goes in the French street

parts.note: rue is French for street, a way
a guy is a man

explanation.surface: An upstanding elderly man charms in the manner of the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the French way' looks like a phrase about Gallic charm, but it is RUE, the French street.
explanation.definitionFit: To charm someone can be to captivate them, making them fall in love, a verb synonym.

clue.text: He rings up about old record

indicators.note: the reversed word goes about, enclosing, the pronoun
in a down clue, up means the letters are read backwards

parts.note: to ring someone is to call them

explanation.surface: A man telephones about a vintage disc.
explanation.definitionFit: Early gramophone discs, the 78s, were pressed from a resin, so the resin's name stands for such a disc.

clue.text: Approving noises from crude fellows with spades?

indicators.note: crude means rough and unrefined, so these words are reworked

parts.note: S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Coarse men with shovels on a building site whistle at passers-by.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude' rearranges FELLOWS WITH into all but the final letter. The whole clue also reads as a description, so it is close to an &lit.
explanation.definitionFit: Two-note whistles directed at an attractive person express admiration, crude approval of looks.

clue.text: 31 days to be included in ordinary credit

indicators.note: the phrase is included in, placed inside, the abbreviations

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit

explanation.surface: A month's worth of days counted as ordinary credit.
explanation.definitionFit: The tenth month of the calendar has thirty-one days, so the length describes it.

clue.text: One born into Middle East group gets sham therapy

indicators.note: the first pieces go into the group's abbreviation

parts.note: PLO is the Palestine Liberation Organization
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A newcomer to a Middle Eastern organisation receives fake treatment.
explanation.definitionFit: An inert pill given for its psychological effect is a dummy treatment with no active ingredient.

clue.text: In declining state, old boy, alone on site, catches cold

parts.note: sole means alone, single

indicators.note: the site word catches, takes inside it, the abbreviation

parts.note: a scene is a place, a site

explanation.surface: An elderly man, on his own at a location, picks up a chill and starts to decline.
explanation.definitionFit: The process of becoming outdated or falling out of use is a condition of decline.

clue.text: Impudent hooker is one

definitions.meaning: in rugby the hooker is a member of the scrum's front pack

explanation.surface: A cheeky prostitute, so the surface claims.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hooker' suggests a prostitute, but it is the rugby position.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: bold and pert in manner, and a player in the rugby pack such as a hooker.

clue.text: Drives ducks in races against the French

indicators.note: against means next to, so the French article follows on
the ducks go in the races

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle races on the Isle of Man
in cricket a duck is a score of nothing, O, so two ducks are OO
les is French for the (plural)

explanation.surface: Someone drives ducks to race them against French competitors.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, so it looks like the letter O.
explanation.definitionFit: To potter along unhurriedly in a car is to motor gently, a light synonym for driving.

clue.text: Guard "hard" border

parts.note: H is the pencil abbreviation for hard
an edge is a border

explanation.surface: A security guard patrolling a tough frontier, a nod to the Brexit 'hard border'.
explanation.definitionFit: To protect yourself against a financial loss is to cover a bet, safeguarding against risk.

clue.text: Heath left behind miners dealing with figures

indicators.note: the following pieces come behind, after, the union

parts.note: NUM is the National Union of Mineworkers, the British miners' union
erica is the botanical name for heath or heather

explanation.surface: Prime Minister Edward Heath left the miners behind while busy with statistics.
explanation.walkthrough: Heath suggests Edward Heath, the 1970s Prime Minister who clashed with the miners, but it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to numbers is the plain adjective sense, figures being digits.

clue.text: One loves rambling into microphone for warlord

indicators.note: the pieces go into the microphone's short form

parts.note: mic is short for microphone
I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: rambling words wander about, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone rambles about love into a microphone on behalf of a warlord.
explanation.definitionFit: Slobodan Milosevic led Serbia through the Balkan wars of the 1990s and was tried for war crimes.

clue.text: It chops round apple in bits

indicators.note: round means turned round, read backwards

parts.note: axes chop, so chops means axes

indicators.note: fruit in bits is broken up, so its letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Someone chops round an apple, cutting it into pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' as a definition is easy to miss: it is old slang, as in 'she's got It'. 'round' reverses the chops word and 'in bits' scrambles the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: 'It' is old slang for physical attractiveness, as in 'she's got it'.

clue.text: Mother quits cosmetics firm for talent show

parts.note: Max Factor is a cosmetics brand
ma is mother

explanation.definitionFit: A British televised singing contest searching for that special quality is the classic example.

clue.text: She, for one, is articulate next to this Parisian

indicators.note: the answer next to the French word makes articulate, so that French word is removed from it

parts.note: to articulate a word is to pronounce it
ce is French for this

explanation.surface: A woman speaks clearly beside a Parisian.
explanation.walkthrough: An unusual subtraction: the clue says that the answer, with the French for 'this' set next to it, means articulate, so that French word comes off the end.
explanation.definitionFit: 'She' is a word standing in place of a noun, an example of that part of speech.

clue.text: Bar art in Paris for privates

'thou art' in French is 'tu es', so art becomes es

explanation.surface: A Paris bar whose art is of a rather private sort.
explanation.definitionFit: Privates is a euphemism for the genitals; the hair region over them is named by the answer.

clue.text: Bird, large one, cracking nut

clue.text: Sort of liberal, proud characters

explanation.walkthrough: 'proud' here means standing up from the surface, as raised dots do.

clue.text: Start to remove grassy area at the front

parts.note: a lea is a meadow, a grassy area
to doff a hat is to remove it

explanation.surface: Begin by clearing the lawn at the front of the house.
explanation.definitionFit: To begin proceedings or go first is to open, a phrasal verb meaning begin.

clue.text: Parasols possibly amusing Joe

parts.note: fun means amusing
GI Joe is a US soldier, so a GI is a Joe

explanation.surface: Sunshades might be good for a laugh, says Joe.
explanation.definitionFit: The parasol mushroom is one example of these spore-bearing organisms.

clue.text: Coach leaves around midnight for border

explanation.definitionFit: The self-finished edge of a woven fabric, which stops it fraying, is an edging.

clue.text: Anger follows sincere Christmas gift

to incense is to anger

explanation.definitionFit: The magi brought the infant Jesus gold, myrrh and an aromatic resin, so it counts as a nativity gift.
